questions.question: Which command installs what the course needs to build and run a FastAPI application?
questions.explanation: FastAPI is the framework, Uvicorn is the server that runs it: both are needed. SQLAlchemy is added later for the database.

questions.question: What is Uvicorn?
options: An ASGI server that runs the FastAPI application
A package that must be imported in main.py to declare routes
The tool that generates the Swagger documentation
questions.explanation: Uvicorn is an ASGI server (Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface). The ORM is SQLAlchemy, validation is Pydantic.

questions.question: In the command below, what does main:app mean?
options: Look for the variable app in the module main (main.py)
Run the function main, then the function app
Use the folder main and the file app.py
Start two applications, main and app
Load the class app from the package main
Use main as the host name and app as the port
questions.explanation: The syntax is module:variable. Uvicorn imports main.py and uses the object stored in its variable app.

questions.question: What does the --reload option do?
options: It restarts the server automatically when the code changes
It is the recommended option in production
It reloads the database on every request
It recreates the tables on every request
questions.explanation: --reload watches the source files and restarts the server on every save. It costs resources and is a development option.

questions.question: By default, at which address does uvicorn main:app serve the application?
questions.explanation: Uvicorn listens on 127.0.0.1, port 8000. localhost is the name of the same address.

questions.question: Uvicorn is launched from a folder that does not contain main.py. What happens?
options: Uvicorn fails to import the module main
The server starts and every route returns 404
Uvicorn searches for main.py in all subfolders
The server starts on another port
questions.explanation: main:app is a Python import: the module must be importable from the current folder, otherwise Uvicorn stops with an import error.

questions.question: What is the difference between WSGI and ASGI?
options: ASGI supports asynchronous code (async/await), WSGI is synchronous
WSGI is required to use FastAPI
questions.explanation: WSGI is the classic synchronous interface (used by Django by default). ASGI is its asynchronous successor, which FastAPI is built on.

questions.question: What does FastAPI() create?
options: A Uvicorn server already listening on port 8000
questions.explanation: app = FastAPI() creates the application. It does not start anything: Uvicorn runs it.

questions.question: What does @app.get("/") do?
options: It declares a route that answers GET requests on /
It also answers POST requests on /
It sends a GET request to /
It answers every HTTP method on /
questions.explanation: The decorator associates the path and the HTTP method with the function. A POST on / would get 405 Method Not Allowed.

questions.question: What does a browser display at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ with this code?
questions.explanation: A returned dict is automatically converted to JSON.

questions.question: What is the response to GET /items/42 with this route?
questions.explanation: Without a type annotation, a path parameter is received as a string, hence the quotes.

questions.question: With the route below, what are the responses to GET /items_type/42 and GET /items_type/abc?
questions.explanation: The annotation int makes FastAPI convert the value and validate it. A value that is not an integer returns 422 with a detailed message.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code does FastAPI return when a parameter fails validation?
questions.explanation: FastAPI returns 422 with a detail list giving the location (path, query, body), the message and the received value.

questions.question: A function parameter does not appear in the route path and is typed int. Where does FastAPI read it from?
questions.explanation: Parameters in {braces} come from the path, simple types not in the path come from the query string, Pydantic models from the body.

questions.question: With the code below, what does GET /items return?
options: A 422 error because limit is missing
questions.explanation: A default value makes the query parameter optional. Without = 10, it would be required and its absence would give 422.

questions.question: Both routes below are declared in this order. What does GET /users/me return?
options: A 422 error: /users/{user_id} matches first and 'me' is not an int
questions.explanation: Routes are tested in declaration order. The fixed route /users/me must be declared before /users/{user_id}.

questions.question: Which statements about async def routes are true?
options: The course routes are declared with async def
FastAPI also accepts plain def routes
async def is mandatory for every FastAPI route
async def makes SQLAlchemy queries asynchronous
A def route cannot return JSON
async def routes cannot take parameters
questions.explanation: Both are accepted. FastAPI runs plain def routes in a thread pool, which is why blocking code (such as synchronous SQLAlchemy) is better placed in def routes.

questions.question: Two route functions are both named read_item. What happens?
options: Both routes work: the decorator registered each function before the name was reused
Both paths call the second function
questions.explanation: The decorator stores the function when it runs, so the second definition only rebinds the Python name. It works, but it is confusing: give each function its own name.

questions.question: Which URLs show the documentation generated automatically by FastAPI?
questions.explanation: Both are generated from the code. /admin is Django's interface, not FastAPI's.

questions.question: Which statements about the /docs page are true?
options: It lets you send real requests to the API with 'Try it out'
It is built from the OpenAPI schema available at /openapi.json
It must be written by hand in a YAML file
It requires installing an extra package
It is only available when --reload is used
questions.explanation: FastAPI describes every route, parameter and schema in /openapi.json; Swagger UI and ReDoc display it.

questions.question: Where does FastAPI get the information shown in the documentation?
options: The type annotations and Pydantic schemas
questions.explanation: The paths, methods, parameter types and body/response schemas all come from the code itself.

questions.question: Which HTTP methods match the CRUD operations Create and Delete?
questions.explanation: Create = POST, Read = GET, Update = PUT (or PATCH), Delete = DELETE.

questions.question: Which statements about a REST API are true?
options: Each resource is identified by a URL
The HTTP method expresses the action (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
It can only be called from a browser
questions.explanation: A REST API exposes resources at URLs and usually exchanges JSON. Any HTTP client can call it.

questions.question: Which method is used to update an existing user in the course?
questions.explanation: @app.put("/user/{user_id}") replaces the user's fields. There is no UPDATE method in HTTP.

questions.question: Which status codes are used correctly?
options: 404 when the requested user does not exist
500 when the client sends an invalid email
404 when the request succeeds but the list is empty
questions.explanation: An empty list is still a success (200). 500 means a server bug, 422 is a validation error, 201 means Created.

questions.question: A route answers GET only. What does a DELETE request on the same path return?
questions.explanation: The path exists but not for this method: 405. A path that does not exist at all gives 404.

questions.question: Which statements about the status code of a POST route are true?
options: By default FastAPI returns 200, including for POST
status_code=201 in the decorator returns 201 Created
A POST route cannot return a body
The status code depends on the function name
questions.explanation: The course routes return 200. @app.post("/adduser", status_code=201) would follow the REST convention.

questions.question: What is SQLAlchemy?
options: A FastAPI plugin that generates the docs
questions.explanation: SQLAlchemy lets you manipulate rows as Python objects. SQLite is the database engine it talks to.

questions.question: What does create_engine(SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URL) create?
options: The engine that manages connections to the database
A session already opened for a request
questions.explanation: The engine holds the connection pool. Sessions are created later from SessionLocal, which is bound to the engine.

questions.question: With the URL below, where is the database stored?
options: In a file test.db in the folder Uvicorn is launched from
In the folder that contains database.py, wherever Uvicorn is launched from
In the folder of the virtual environment
questions.explanation: sqlite:/// is followed by a relative path: ./test.db is relative to the current directory, not to the file database.py.

questions.question: What is SessionLocal?
options: A factory: SessionLocal() creates a new session
A function that closes the database
A single shared session for the whole application
questions.explanation: sessionmaker returns a class. Each call to SessionLocal() gives a new session, one per request in get_db.

questions.question: With autocommit=False, what is needed for changes to be saved in the database?
options: Nothing: every db.add() is saved immediately
questions.explanation: The changes stay in a transaction until commit(). Without it, they are lost when the session is closed.

questions.question: What is Base, created with declarative_base()?
options: The base class that every model inherits from
An instance of the User model
The base URL of the API
questions.explanation: class User(Base) registers the table in Base.metadata, which create_all uses.

questions.question: The course imports declarative_base from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative. Which statements are true with SQLAlchemy 2.x?
options: The import still works but emits a deprecation warning
The recommended import is from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
declarative_base no longer exists at all
It must be imported from fastapi
It must be imported from pydantic
questions.explanation: Since SQLAlchemy 2.0 the function lives in sqlalchemy.orm. The old path emits MovedIn20Warning.

questions.question: What does __tablename__ = "users" define?
options: The name of the table in the database
The URL prefix of the user routes
The name of the Pydantic schema
The name of the Python class
The name of the database file
questions.explanation: ForeignKey refers to the table name, while relationship refers to the class name.

questions.question: Which statements about this column are true?
options: It is the primary key of the table
index=True creates an index on it
Its value must be given when creating a User
It is optional and usually NULL
questions.explanation: An Integer primary key is filled automatically by SQLite (1, 2, 3...). The index speeds up lookups by id.

questions.question: What does unique=True on the email column imply?
options: Two users cannot have the same email
Inserting a duplicate raises an IntegrityError at commit
Pydantic checks that the email is unique
The email becomes the primary key
FastAPI returns 409 automatically on a duplicate
questions.explanation: The database enforces the constraint. In the course code the exception is not caught, so the client gets a 500 error.

questions.question: Which statements about nullable are true in SQLAlchemy?
options: A column that is not a primary key is nullable by default
nullable=True on url is therefore redundant
Columns are NOT NULL by default
nullable=False makes the field optional in Pydantic
nullable only applies to Integer columns
A primary key is nullable by default
questions.explanation: Column(String) already accepts NULL. nullable=False is what must be written explicitly, for example for a foreign key that is required.

questions.question: What does Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) do?
options: It creates the tables of every model that inherits from Base
It leaves tables that already exist untouched
It deletes and recreates every table
It adds new columns to existing tables
questions.explanation: create_all only creates missing tables. A column added to an existing model is not added to the table: delete test.db or use a migration tool (Alembic).

questions.question: A column is added to the User model after test.db was created. The server is restarted. What happens?
options: The column is not created: create_all skips the existing users table
The users table is recreated empty
FastAPI adds the column at the first request
questions.explanation: Unlike Django's migrate, create_all does not alter existing tables. Queries on the new column will then fail.

questions.question: What is a Pydantic schema such as UserSchema used for?
options: Validating the data received in the request body
Describing the shape of the data returned by the API
Creating the table in the database
questions.explanation: Pydantic validates and converts the data. The table is described by the SQLAlchemy model, which is a different class.

questions.question: Which fields are required in this schema?
questions.code:
class UserSchema(BaseModel):
    name: str
    email: str
    nickname: str
    url: Optional[str] = None
questions.explanation: name, email and nickname have no default value: they are required. url has the default None, so it can be omitted.

questions.question: In Pydantic 2, which statements about a field declared url: Optional[str] (without = None) are true?
options: It accepts None as a value
It is still required: the key must be present
It can be omitted from the JSON
questions.explanation: Optional[str] means 'str or None'. What makes a field optional is the default value: url: Optional[str] = None.

questions.question: A client sends this JSON to POST /adduser. What happens?
options: FastAPI returns 422 because nickname is missing
The detail of the error points to the missing field
The user is created with nickname = None
The user is created with nickname = ""
The server crashes with a 500 error
questions.explanation: Validation happens before the function runs: the route code is never executed.

questions.question: In Pydantic 2, which inputs pass validation for a field age: int?
questions.explanation: In lax mode Pydantic converts "42" to 42 and 4.0 to 4, but refuses any value that would lose information or is not a number.

questions.question: In Pydantic 2, a client sends {"name": 123, ...} for a field name: str. What happens?
options: Validation fails with 422: an int is not converted to str
questions.explanation: Pydantic 2 converts strings to numbers but not numbers to strings.

questions.question: What does orm_mode = True (from_attributes = True in Pydantic 2) allow?
options: Building the schema from an object's attributes, such as a SQLAlchemy User
Creating the table in the database
questions.explanation: Without it, Pydantic expects a dict. FastAPI can also convert ORM objects returned by a route with a response_model.

questions.question: The course schema uses class Config: orm_mode = True. Which statements are true with Pydantic 2?
options: The modern spelling is model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
Pydantic 2 no longer supports ORM objects
orm_mode is now mandatory on every schema
questions.explanation: The old spelling still works but emits warnings: 'orm_mode' has been renamed to 'from_attributes', and class-based config is deprecated.

questions.question: Why is a Pydantic schema separate from the SQLAlchemy model?
options: The model describes the table, the schema describes the data exchanged with the client
The client must not send fields such as id, which the database generates
SQLAlchemy models cannot be imported in main.py
questions.explanation: Separating them lets the API choose what is accepted (input) and what is exposed (output), independently from the storage.

questions.question: What does db: Session = Depends(get_db) do in a route?
options: FastAPI calls get_db and passes the session it yields to the route
The session is created once when the server starts
The client must send the session in the body
It opens a single session at startup
questions.explanation: Depends is dependency injection: FastAPI resolves the dependency for each request.

questions.question: In get_db, what is the role of yield?
options: It gives the session to the route
The code after yield (the finally) runs once the request is handled
It returns the session and ends the function immediately
It turns the function into a coroutine
It makes the function run in parallel
questions.explanation: A dependency with yield works like a context manager: setup before yield, cleanup (db.close()) after.

questions.question: Why is db.close() inside a finally block?
options: The session is closed even if the route raises an exception
Without finally, the route is never called
questions.explanation: An HTTPException raised in the route still goes through finally, so the connection is always returned to the pool.

questions.question: What happens with Depends(get_db()) instead of Depends(get_db)?
options: Depends expects the function itself, not the result of a call
FastAPI raises a TypeError as soon as the route is defined
The same session is shared by every request
questions.explanation: get_db() returns a generator object, which is not callable: 'is not a callable object'. FastAPI must call the dependency itself, once per request.

questions.question: In add_user(url: Request, request: UserSchema, ...), how does FastAPI know what to inject?
options: From the type annotations, not the parameter names
url receives the Request object because it is annotated Request
From the parameter names: url must be a URL string
request receives the Request object because of its name
From the order of the parameters
questions.explanation: The names are confusing in the course (url is the Request, request is the body). FastAPI only looks at the types.

questions.question: What does request.base_url contain in the course routes?
options: The root URL of the API, such as http://127.0.0.1:8000/
A value used to build each user's url field
The full URL including the path /adduser
The IP address of the client only
questions.explanation: f"{url.base_url}user/{request.name}" gives http://127.0.0.1:8000/user/alice.

questions.question: In which order are these calls made to save a new user and get its id?
questions.explanation: add puts the object in the session, commit writes it, refresh reloads it from the database (with the generated id).

questions.question: Which statements are true before db.commit() is called?
options: After db.add(user), user.id is still None
Nothing has been saved in the database yet
user.id is already set by db.add()
The row is visible to other sessions
db.add() raises an error if the email already exists
questions.explanation: The id is generated by the database during the INSERT, which happens at flush/commit.

questions.question: What does db.query(User).all() return?
options: None if the table is empty
questions.explanation: all() always returns a list. FastAPI then converts it to JSON using the response_model.

questions.question: What does db.query(User).filter(User.name == "bob").first() return if no user is named bob?
questions.explanation: first() returns None. In the course route GET /user/{user_name}, FastAPI then sends null with status 200: you have to raise HTTPException yourself.

questions.question: Why is filter written with == and not =?
options: User.name == value builds a SQL condition
= is an assignment and would be a syntax error inside the call
questions.explanation: SQLAlchemy overloads == on columns to produce a WHERE clause instead of a boolean.

questions.question: Which calls delete a user from the database?
questions.explanation: del only removes the Python variable. db.delete marks the row, commit executes the DELETE.

questions.question: In the PUT route, why is there no db.add(user) before db.commit()?
options: The user was loaded by the session, which already tracks its changes
Modifying its attributes is enough for commit to issue an UPDATE
The modification is saved by refresh
questions.explanation: Objects loaded through db.query are attached to the session. db.add would not create a duplicate, it is simply unnecessary.

questions.question: How should a route signal that a user does not exist?
questions.explanation: HTTPException must be raised, not returned. The client receives {"detail": "..."} with the given status.

questions.question: The course DELETE route declares user_id: str. What does DELETE /user/abc return?
options: 404: the query finds no user with that id
No 422 is returned because any string is a valid str
questions.explanation: With user_id: int (as in PUT), FastAPI would reject abc with 422 before querying the database.

questions.question: What does response_model=list[UserSchema] do?
options: It declares that the route returns a list of users
It converts the users to XML
It makes the route return HTML
It sorts the users by name
questions.explanation: The response model also appears in the documentation as the response schema.

questions.question: In the course, GET /users uses response_model=list[UserSchema]. Which statements are true?
options: The id of each user is not in the response, because UserSchema has no id field
Fields not declared in the response model are removed
The id is always added automatically
The response contains every column of the table
The users are returned without the url field
questions.explanation: This is why a separate output schema with id (UserOut in the corrected code) is needed to call PUT /user/{id} or DELETE /user/{id}.

questions.question: Why can response_model be useful for security?
options: It prevents sensitive columns (a password hash, for example) from being returned
Only the fields of the schema are sent to the client
questions.explanation: Even if the ORM object has more attributes, only those declared in the response model are serialized.

questions.question: A user can publish several posts, a post belongs to only one user. Where is the foreign key?
options: In the posts table: user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"))
On the 'many' side of the relationship
questions.explanation: One-to-many: each post stores the id of its author. An association table is needed only for many-to-many.

questions.question: What does relationship("Post", back_populates="author") add to the User model?
options: An attribute user.posts that lists the user's Post objects
No new column in the users table
A new column posts in the users table
A foreign key in the users table
questions.explanation: relationship is Python-side only. The column is the ForeignKey in posts. back_populates links user.posts and post.author.

questions.question: In ForeignKey("users.id") and relationship("Post"), what do the strings refer to?
questions.explanation: A ForeignKey points to a table column, a relationship points to a mapped class.

questions.question: Why is user_id declared with nullable=False on Post?
options: A post must always have an author
Inserting a post without user_id fails
It makes user_id the primary key
It is the default, so it changes nothing
It deletes the posts of a deleted user
questions.explanation: Columns are nullable by default, so the constraint has to be explicit. Deleting posts with their author is the job of cascade.

questions.question: With cascade="all, delete-orphan" on User.posts, what happens when a user is deleted with db.delete(user)?
options: The user's posts are deleted too
No post is left pointing to a deleted user
The posts are kept with user_id = None
The deletion is refused while posts exist
Only the first post is deleted
questions.explanation: Without a cascade, SQLAlchemy would try to set user_id to NULL, which nullable=False forbids.

questions.question: Which routes are a sound design for the posts exercise?
options: POST /addpost with title, content and user_id in the body
GET /user/{user_id}/posts to list the posts of a user
questions.explanation: The method gives the action: POST creates, GET reads, PUT updates, DELETE deletes.

questions.question: Which statements about foreign keys in SQLite are true?
options: SQLite does not enforce foreign keys unless PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is executed
Without it, a post could reference a user id that does not exist
Foreign keys only work with Integer primary keys named pk
PRAGMA foreign_keys deletes the existing tables
questions.explanation: The corrected code enables the PRAGMA on every connection, and POST /addpost also checks the user exists to return a clean 404.

questions.question: Why must the server check that the user exists before creating a post?
options: To return a clear 404 instead of a database error
Because the client can send any user_id
It is only needed for GET routes
questions.explanation: Pydantic only checks that user_id is an int. Whether that user exists is a database question.
